## installer-v0.1.0 — the first build of the wizard

Emulatarr stands up a self-hosted retro game library on your NAS. It runs on
your PC, connects over SSH, and deploys the RomM stack (RomM, MariaDB, Valkey)
on the other end. Nothing installs locally.

Six screens: Welcome, Connect, Detect, Configure, Run, Done.

**What it handles for you**

- SSH with password or key, and the privilege escalation worked out per NAS. Sudo passwords are masked at a fixed width before they reach the screen or the log, so the length doesn't leak either.
- One batched probe that reports platform, architecture, container runtime, free space, and whether the web port is already taken, before anything is written.
- A form that becomes a `.env` deterministically, with values quoted against an allow-list, because the NAS side sources that file.
- The folder layout with the right `PUID`/`PGID` and Synology ACLs, skipping the slow recursive pass unless you ask for it.
- The install itself, streamed back live, with a step rail that tracks it and a health check at the end.
- Per-NAS profiles, encrypted at rest, exportable as a passphrase-wrapped file.

**Updating**

The wizard polls GitHub Releases, shows a **New version** banner, and applies
the update on **Restart & install**. It verifies the download by size and
sha256 first. Saved profiles in `%APPDATA%\emulatarr-installer\` survive.

---

**Download:** `emulatarr-installer-win-unpacked.zip` — extract anywhere on your
Windows machine and run `Emulatarr Installer.exe`. Nothing is installed
locally; the wizard drives your NAS over SSH. SmartScreen may warn on first
run since the build is unsigned.

Prefer to skip the wizard? It uploads exactly
[`nas/scripts/`](https://github.com/defessler/Emulatarr-releases/tree/main/nas/scripts),
which lives in this repo. Copy that folder to your NAS and run `setup.sh`
yourself — see
[`QUICKSTART.md`](https://github.com/defessler/Emulatarr-releases/blob/main/QUICKSTART.md).
It's a supported route, not a fallback.

Page: https://dougfessler.com/projects/emulatarr/
